findings.summary: Two expected-best attacks were interrupted by modeled damage variance: Lildozer fell before its second Bulldoze and Croakatoa fell to an explicit critical hit.
findings.observed_fact: Both actions were selected from unsafe states to make progress before faint; Croakatoa still left Ponyta at the 3-HP fresh-Fake-Out threshold.
findings.strategic_judgment: Neither faint invalidated the role sequence or exposed a verified safer continuation; the unchanged policy adapted and retained three healthy matchup roles at that point.
findings.next_test: Monitor Clone 3 for terminal success across another damage branch without adding variance-specific trainer rules.

findings.summary: Healthy Bugatti was spent in a locked three-turn Rollout sequence against Dustox.
findings.observed_fact: Rollout trapped and fainted Bugatti but softened Dustox enough for a hit-free Birdlaw finish. The sole material alternative was replayed once: Birdlaw switched safely, then a critical Venoshock left it at 3 HP while Dustox remained at 29 HP.
findings.strategic_judgment: The Birdlaw pivot did not lexicographically dominate this fixed branch; sacrificing Bugatti preserved the faster Dustox and Sunflora finisher at 41 terminal HP. Classification remains expected-best, not forced or proven.
findings.next_test: Retain the thresholded Rollout exception and require Birdlaw to enter productively after Bugatti in any matching branch.

findings.summary: Ohmnomnom fainted after taking over the Eelektrik line, but removed most of Eelektrik and preserved Bushtank for the endgame.
findings.observed_fact: Fresh Fake Out plus four Sparks reduced Eelektrik for Bugatti Bug Bite; Bushtank survived the battle at 15 HP rather than being consumed as in Clone 1.
findings.strategic_judgment: This is a productive role conversion, not switch spam; the policy adapted to the one-Spark Bibarel branch and different trainer sendout order.
findings.next_test: Verify the policy can choose either the Bushtank-sacrifice or Ohmnomnom-converter branch without a no-action relay.

findings.summary: Seven switches occurred and none formed an immediate reversal or consecutive voluntary no-action loop.
findings.observed_fact: Three were forced replacements; the voluntary switches assigned Lildozer to Ponyta, Bushtank then Ohmnomnom to Eelektrik, and every entrant acted before leaving or fainting.
findings.strategic_judgment: The sequence demonstrates dynamic role reuse across a different sendout order rather than hard-coded turn numbers.
findings.next_test: Repeat the switch audit after Clone 3.

findings.summary: The adaptive branch won in 25 certified actions, four fewer than Clone 1.
findings.observed_fact: Eighteen move choices and seven switches ended with Bushtank at 15 HP and Birdlaw at 41 HP.
findings.strategic_judgment: The shorter win is useful evidence that the same declarative bundle handles RNG-driven roster order without profile rewrites.
findings.next_test: Do not optimize further unless Clone 3 reveals a dominated action.

findings.summary: A one-Spark Bibarel KO changed Gavi next sendout and the policy still completed without stale turn assumptions.
findings.observed_fact: The opponent order became Ponyta, Eelektrik, Dustox, Sunflora rather than Clone 1 order, while every chosen action remained legal and verified.
findings.strategic_judgment: This is positive evidence for state-predicate reuse over scripted action lists.
findings.next_test: Require Clone 3 to remain state-driven under whichever verified sendout order occurs.

correct_choices: All 25 actions and the terminal reward were RAM-verified with zero execution discrepancies.
Fake Out was used only on fresh entries at turns 6, 10, and 14.
The policy handled a different enemy sendout order under the same behavior hash without turn-number rules.
The bounded Birdlaw alternative was tested once and rejected on observed evidence rather than intuition.
